descriptionChirho: Death as the cessation of physical life, whether natural or violent. The single core lexical meaning of θάνατος across all its NT occurrences (120 tokens). Uniformly rendered Ger. 'Tod,' Fr. 'mort,' Heb. 'מָוֶת,' Kor. '죽음,' Hin. 'मृत्यु,' Spa. 'muerte,' Arb. 'المَوْتِ.' The auto-clusters 'of death,' 'by death,' 'deaths,' and 'death' are merely case-inflected forms (genitive θανάτου, dative θανάτῳ, accusative θάνατον, plural θανάτοις) of the same meaning, not distinct senses. Used of: Christ's death (Matt 20:18, 26:38/66, Mark 10:33, 14:34/64, Luke 22:33, John 12:33, 18:32, 21:19, Phil 2:27), physical death generally (Matt 4:16, Luke 1:79, 2:26, 9:27, Heb 7:23, 11:5), the realm/power of death (Matt 16:28 'shadow of death'), and multiple mortal perils (2 Cor 11:23 θανάτοις plural). All map to one semantic domain: the end of biological life.
